author: Legoche
body:
Incoming Rant. If you read it all you will understand more.

The community is dying. We get occasional players in game, but the solid community who are active on the forums and on teamspeak are dying. Nowadays, going on teamspeak, there are 3 players, 2 in the afk channel, one playing Kohi. Right now typing this post, there are 11 people online on the forums. Alot of the old players don't come online nowadays unless they are scrimming. Public Avicus is just dying. I went on earlier today, and played some public Avicus. The map: A Quintus that had been playing for 50 minutes because of stalemate defenders. After that, Senex 1, a 6 minute match, then, Haunted Halloween map, another 10 minute match. Everybody plays throwback nowadays, and nebula in general. I love other gamemodes such as Walls, Nexus, CTH, but these gamemodes are never played. On Avicus, what is there to work for? I play for hours grinding credits, for what? I disagree with Prestiges, but back when they were in, there was SOMETHING to work for. Now it is just about saving for a badge, or a pet that nobody will see. We need more events for the community. For example, Robo UHCs. What was it, 50 players in one teamspeak channel at once? What about the unofficial tournaments? The player count rocketed. Players want to see more Competitive gamemodes and not a new arcade gamemode that nobody will play. If you want to fix public avicus, make something GOOD to work towards. Please, start doing something about public. Throwback Nebula gets soooo old. I think that a double xp week on a different server may work, but please do something!

I hope this isn't going to turn into another "Avicus Is Dying Post" that doesn't get any support from Developers, just like these:

https://avicus.net/forums/48b250e1a

https://avicus.net/forums/fc860ea17

Please do something, thanks, Lego.

replies.author: gobernment
replies.body:
My two cents:

1: The problems with TeamSpeak
Probably our most controversial service. I have a few suggestions for combating this;

- Reintroduce private channels. We should have not removed them, they were fine before. It would especially be useful for scrimmages and such, in the case that it is not around tournament time. It would allow users to properly have conversations on there, but invite their own friends in, and not really have a huge focus on the rules. I suppose having the user be responsible for their channel's content would make more sense.

- Official, straightforward rules. TeamSpeak is used a lot for "rule loopholes", or how the staff are accused of setting up certain players to fail. If we addressed certain situations, certain rules, and revised wordings to make them less confusing or more based on common sense instead of tossing our hat in at things that are just questionable, I think it's worthy of time to draft new rules for TeamSpeak that haven't been done before. The rules seem inconsistent and flaky in their current state.

- More reliable hosting. TeamSpeak is targeted primarily for it's features in things such as tournament operation and staff meetings. Occasionally, when something is scheduled, the TeamSpeak may go down. It seems that because of this, TeamSpeak also may go down for hours to days at a time, or it'll just be wiped/reverted. It's not really stable enough and it's not maintained well, so I don't see the problem with upping it if it's one of the few things that we provide for the regulars.

2: Focusing too much on new players
I think I've noticed a pattern: we are kind of turning into a lower-end server because we focus more on new players that we don't have, and not focusing on the players we currently have. Nothing appeals to the older players: the donators probably have the worst end of it. They lost all their perks, and the only perks now they have are the rank and the suites on TS: the ability to join full games and pick teams in full games was removed, and the things such as the shop and website have strayed away to the opposite of what community feedback demanded.

I personally think if we've set on players for so long, and they're not coming for an advertising plan (so as to what the former admins have tried to set up, but failed), we shouldn't continue trying to proof the server having a newbie-focused environment. We should do with what we have for now, and, if something is set in stone, work off of that. We've seen a lot of our community members leave because of how the server has ended up, and it's because action hasn't properly been taken. I don't want to say it's all based on nostalgia; because it's not.

The "regulars" are regulars, and are part of our community: they're alienated between newer players. The "regulars" are what keeps us running, especially financially. Can't see I've seen so many new players donating recently.

3: Lack of proper administration cycle
We're going through admins too much. We've lost so many within the past 6 months: it's obvious there needs to be a change, and I don't think there's much that we've shun light upon for fixing it. I'll assume, say, that most of it is because of pressure and stress. From what I can tell, it's been poor working conditions for the administrators. While some have had differing retirement reasons, there's a lot of problems that aren't needed. I've always thought we could explore our options to when it wasn't a problem: maybe readd the manager rank; or, we could get a third admin to not have stress on just two and get that "extra opinion" since Kylo isn't really one for executive decisions like the others; we could possibly, also, just completely change the format of administrator, and have one whole "senior" team that manage things, instead of a hierarchy. Whatever could work, we need to explore options. We're stuck on that regard

replies.author: LeCobalt
replies.body:
This is the real reason:

The "Avicus" update came in with a few tweaks and changes to the game-modes. I honestly don't remember them that well, but within them an aspect was removed. A very very important aspect. Advertising stopped. In MC Zone players were given a free kit for one day if they voted on the server list. It was the reason I joined this server. 

MC Zone was in the first page for like a week. This is how it grew. Over half a million of players joined MC Zone. On a normal day, at a normal time, MC Zone had around 2000 players online. There were 4 nebula matches. There was just one lobby filled up with players, fun and simple to understand. 

Of course, one might think "Players left in MC Zone too you dummy:P", and I'd completely agree with them. The only difference is that people kept on joining on MC Zone. The amount of people joining compared to those leaving was way greater. Thousands of new players joined the servers every day, the home screen even said that.

AVICUS would've kicked MC Zone's ass if Avicus would've promoted itself through votes on server lists, like this one: http://minecraftservers.org/  

I joined this server right after it changed from walls over too MC Zone. It was a part of my life. Please tell this to funky.
